results.title: Hyperbolic multi-channel hypergraph convolutional neural network based on multilayer hypergraph | Scientific Reports
results.content: In summary, although significant progress has been made in hypergraph modeling, multi-channel mechanisms, and hyperbolic embedding, there is a lack of a graph neural network framework that can uniformly model multilayer high-order structures, integrate multiple structural perspectives, and adapt to non-Euclidean geometric spaces. To fill this gap, this paper proposes a Hyperbolic Multi-channel HyperGraph Neural Network (HMHGNN), which systematically integrates three types of structure-aware channels: derivative graph, line graph, and hyperbolic convolutions, and collaboratively models the internal dependencies of hyperedges, the interactions between hyperedges, and the global hierarchical topology, so as to better serve the node classification and link prediction goals in complex tasks. Although hypergraph neural networks have achieved remarkable results in tasks such as node classification, link prediction, and graph classification, existing methods are mostly limited to singlelayer hypergraph modeling, and it is difficult to effectively capture high-order relationships and inter-layer interactions in multilayer hypergraph.

results.title: Hypergraph neural network for remote sensing hyperspectral image super-resolution - ScienceDirect
results.content: # Hypergraph neural network for remote sensing hyperspectral image super-resolution. With the thriving development of deep learning, the hyperspectral image (HSI) super-resolution (SR) technology has made significant progress. Existing methods often ignore the task orientation of network learning and the global distribution characteristics of the structural and semantic features in images, leading to spatial and spectral distortions. To address these issues and achieve a more comprehensive information representation, we propose a feature fusion method based on a hypergraph neural network and convolutional neural network (HG-CNet). Specifically, we constructed a three-layer hypergraph based on texture features (T), spectral clustering (S), and positional relationships (P), called TSP, and designed a hypergraph attention module (HGAM). In addition, we constructed a multi-order spatial interaction module (MSIM) to realize cross-guidance and fusion of different types of features in the network. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first application of hypergraph neural networks for solving an HSI SR task.
